canonical_definition: Visual Question Answering (VQA) is a behavior involving the integration of visual inputs (images or videos) and associated textual information to generate answers to questions, often requiring reasoning over multimodal content. The task typically involves open-ended or closed-set question-answering formats, with outputs ranging from free-text responses to selected options, and is frequently used to assess capabilities in multimodal understanding, instruction following, and general reasoning. Variants include biomedical, remote sensing, and temporally grounded VQA (e.g., video-based tasks requiring localization), with some papers framing it as a benchmark for evaluating models' ability to chain interconnected facts or handle hallucination tendencies.
